correctness.rationale: The exact 2-domination and 2-sharp neighborhood-difference characterization is independently stated in Jean–Seo (2022), Theorem 2.1. For matched same-shore indices i!=j, the exclusive neighborhoods are {a_i,b_j} and {a_j,b_i}, forcing at most one omitted matched vertex per shore and forbidding a doubly omitted deleted pair. An unmatched vertex forces itself and all matched vertices of the opposite shore. The complete list of remaining candidates is evaluated using the exact adjacent-pair exclusives B\{b_i,b_j} and A\{a_i,a_j}, yielding the t=3,4,5 boundaries and all coefficients. Cases of two unmatched vertices on a shore are ruled out by twin exclusive differences; all t<=2 cases have either an undominated vertex or a triangle-free edge with both endpoints degree at most two. Standalone direct-neighborhood enumeration checked 155 bounded parameter triples, and constructive witnesses for 32 larger families.

originality.rationale: A full inspection of the original Jean–Seo (2022) manuscript establishes the criterion and general complexity, hypercube, cubic and infinite-grid results, but not these partial-matching-deletion biclique code polynomials. Seo–Slater (2018) provides the general separating-system framework, not an inspected matching-deletion enumeration. A separately published theorem on ordinary identifying codes of thick chain graphs uses a weaker code invariant on a different graph class, and previously described matching-deleted biclique results count other invariants (CIS pairs, domination, colorings), not 2-sharp detecting codes. Searches by equivalent terminology, all-code distributions, exact graph family and optimal 2t-2/t(t-1) parameters revealed no equivalent or stronger covering result. Residual publication-priority limitations are recorded explicitly.
residual_risks: The journal version of the closest 2022 full manuscript was not independently read in full, leaving any later unindexed family-specific addition unresolved.
The full 2018 generalized separating-systems article was not obtained; only its attributed general criterion and metadata were assessed.
Highly specialized results not indexed by the available searches could subsume the family enumeration; independent publication-priority confirmation has not occurred.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of a full three-parameter family of dense bipartite graphs obtained by deleting matching edges. It counts all valid sets, not merely a minimum, and exhibits a sharp quadratic/linear/unique/zero spectrum as the numbers of unmatched vertices change, together with exact small-order thresholds and sensor fractions tending to one in crown graphs. The structural forcing mechanism describes genuinely model-specific false-negative robustness, not a relabelling of ordinary identifying or dominating sets. No larger downstream result is required for the precise complete census to be mathematically valuable.
